summary: A nonzero inner product has a coset c with both coordinates nonzero; the two nonzero phases give u, v ∈ 𝖴 with x a_c⁻¹ ∈ u⁻¹K(g) and y a_c⁻¹ ∈ v⁻¹K(g), whence the claims.

steps.claim: Both phases are nonzero: v, u ∈ 𝖴 with v⁻¹(x a_c⁻¹) ∈ K(g) and u⁻¹(y a_c⁻¹) ∈ K(g).
steps.lean:
have ⟨⟨v, q, f⟩, u, p, g⟩ := (mul_ne_zero_iff.1 f).imp exists_besselU_of_phase_ne_zero
    (exists_besselU_of_phase_ne_zero ∘ star_ne_zero.1)

steps.claim: Take v⁻¹, u⁻¹: v⁻¹x ∈ K (K(g)·a_c ⊆ K since a_c ∈ Z ≤ K) and (v⁻¹x)⁻¹(u⁻¹y) ∈ K(g) (K normalises K(g)).
steps.lean:
⟨_, inv_mem p, _,
    inv_mem q, by simpa using mul_mem (unitaryLevel_le_unitaryLevel_one g) (Z.2.2 c.out.2),
    by simpa using unitaryLevel_one_le_normalizer (Z.2.2 c.out⁻¹.2) (mul_mem (inv_mem g) f)⟩
